This matches the short-form criteria exactly: atomic (one file), local, reversible (one-command revert), and covered (existing focused test). Full plan sections aren't warranted.

## Implementation Plan

### Short form

- **Change**: Fix the formatter bug in the single affected file — correct the faulty formatting logic without touching adjacent formatting rules or call sites.
- **Proof**: Run the existing focused test for this formatter behavior; it should fail before the fix and pass after. No new test needed unless the fix reveals an uncovered edge case in the same code path — if so, extend the existing test rather than adding a new file.
- **Revert**: The known one-command revert restores prior behavior immediately if the fix regresses something downstream (e.g., snapshot mismatches in consumers of the formatter output).

Full-plan sections omitted: atomic, local, reversible, covered change.

If you can point me to the specific file and test (or the bug symptom), I'll apply the fix directly rather than staying at the plan level.
